findings.description: The wrapper now reuses one statistics dict across all calls and clears it at the start of each call, so concurrent threads calling the same decorated function share and clobber one dict.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same @retry-decorated function at once. Mechanism: each call clears the shared dict and the copy writes attempt stats into that same object, so one thread's counters are reset or mixed with another's. Impact: statistics read from the wrapper (or from a thread's copy) show wrong attempt counts and timings. The previous code gave each call its own dict.

findings.description: The async wrapper clears and reuses one shared statistics dict across calls, so overlapping coroutines on the same decorated function interfere with each other's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two tasks await the same decorated coroutine concurrently. Mechanism: the second call's stats.clear() resets the dict while the first call is still retrying, and both copies write into that same dict. Impact: the first call's statistics (attempt_number, idle_for, etc.) are silently reset or corrupted, and wrapped.statistics reflects an arbitrary mix of calls. Previously each call had an isolated dict.
